answer.reason: The verses state several deeds of Titus beyond the companion relation in the summary, including his comforting visit to Corinth, his charge over the collection, and his being left in Crete.

clauses.english: comforted Paul by bringing news of the Corinthians' longing and zeal for him
clauses.quote: God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;

clauses.english: went to Corinth of his own accord to finish the collection for the saints
clauses.quote: of his own accord he went unto you.

clauses.english: was not compelled to be circumcised, being a Greek
clauses.quote: neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised

clauses.english: was left in Crete to set things in order and ordain elders in every city
clauses.quote: left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city

doubts: TIT 3:15 and 2CO 13:14 are subscription notes, not used.
The collection clause relies on 2CO 8:6 and 8:17 together; the 'grace' is later identified as the gift for the saints in verses not shown in full (2CO 8:4).
